title: mkproj is defined in 13 test files and not in the module registered to own it
body:
`MODULES.md:67` registers `tests/lib/test_helper.bash` as THE module for BATS shared test helpers -- *"temp-dir isolation, fixture projects, assertions"*. `mkproj` builds fixture projects. It is defined in **13 test files** and in none of them.

## Measured

Thirteen files each carry their own `mkproj()`:

    data.bats  optin.bats  buildfmt.bats  help.bats  clean.bats  review.bats
    builtins.bats  run_referent.bats  docs.bats  contract.bats  surfaces.bats
    version.bats  dispatch.bats

Sampled four -- `data`, `help`, `clean`, `docs` -- and the bodies are **byte-identical**:

    mkproj() {
      local name="${1:-demo}" proj
      proj="$(create_test_project "$name")"
      install_devbin "$proj"
      cat >"$proj/bin/.devbin/config.yaml"
      echo "$proj"
    }

Four lines over `create_test_project` + `install_devbin`, both of which the registered owner does define.

## The part that makes it more than a tidy-up

**`test_helper.bash` DISCUSSES `mkproj` as though it lived there.** Two of its comment blocks reason about it -- *"the suite was the largest producer of the banned shape; `mkproj` builds under..."* and *"fixed inside `mkproj` -- callers consume it as `proj="$(mkproj ...)"`"*. The owner documents the behaviour of a function it does not contain, so a reader following `MODULES.md` to the registered module finds prose about `mkproj` and no `mkproj`.

**The breach is already known and is already shaping new code.** `tests/unit/shellinit.bats` opens by refusing to add a fourteenth copy:

> `mkproj` IS DELIBERATELY NOT USED HERE. It is a four-line wrapper over `create_test_project` + `install_devbin` that has been copied into 13 test files, against MODULES.md:67 [...] A 14th copy would make a known Highlander breach worse to save two lines, so this file calls the registered helpers directly.

That is the right call for one file and it does not scale: the next author reaches for `mkproj` because twelve neighbours have it, and the honest workaround is invisible unless you open that particular file.

## Why identical copies still matter

They are identical **today**. Highlander is not a rule about tidiness; it is about what happens when one copy is fixed. A `create_test_project` change needing a `mkproj` adjustment lands in one file and the suite stays green, because the other twelve keep working right up until they do not. Thirteen copies is thirteen places to remember.

## Suggested shape, not a decision

Define `mkproj` once in `tests/lib/test_helper.bash` and delete the thirteen. The stdin-consuming `cat >` in the body is the one wrinkle worth thinking about before moving it -- the helper's own comment already reasons about that, which is further evidence of where it belongs.
